body:
Shipped D3+D2, then caught and fixed two real problems before calling it done -- full honesty on both:

SHIPPED: WARRANT#167 (D3) seeds g_Risk.minRisk/maxRisk at init (1.0/15.0, matching what the dead CalculateIntelligentRisk would have set) -- fixes the Kelly ceiling's "no edge" floor silently being 0. WARRANT#168 (D2) wires PredictPatternFormation/ForecastRegimeChanges/UpdateNeuralNetworkSimulation into the live per-bar update block (their own guard clauses verified satisfied at that call site) and flips predictiveSystem.predictionsValid true once they run -- activates an already-built, already-consumed predictive subsystem that was permanently gated off.

CAUGHT PROBLEM 1: the V-4/V-5 reachability tool I built has a real bug -- it misses any function with a custom struct return type, which corrupted its reachability analysis for everything after those functions. This produced ONE wrong disclosure that had already shipped: AnalyzeMarketStructure() was marked dead/superseded when it's actually live (called via CalculateMarketFeatures(), ~120 call sites). Retracted and corrected in-source. Every other finding from this week (A, C, D1-D4) was independently re-verified with a method not affected by the bug and confirmed correct -- only that one was wrong.

CAUGHT PROBLEM 2: after shipping D3+D2, a compile got denied by the permission classifier, my retry skipped a step and compiled a stale cached copy instead, then I propagated that stale copy back over the real edits -- silently losing WARRANT#167/168 for a few minutes. Caught by grepping for the warrant markers in the "shipped" file and finding zero. Re-applied both, compiled correctly this time (single atomic step, verified present before propagating), redeployed byte-identical.

Everything is now correct and verified: 0 errors/0 warnings, WARRANT#166/167/168 all confirmed present in all 3 deployed copies, forge_ledger.json/ARGUS ledger/capability register all updated with the fixes AND the corrections. The V-4/V-5 tool's capability-register entry is downgraded to "known bug, hand-verify every lead" until it's rewritten -- I'm not going to keep trusting its raw output for new findings.

On "the latest agents for precision every line": that ambition is real but a full multi-agent forge-family sweep (the "smith tungsten" roster) is its own multi-hour campaign, not something to compress into this reply on top of everything above. Want me to launch that as the next thing, or hold here for tonight?
